clue.text: Bird a short distance behind guy

indicators.note: behind places the short distance after the guy

parts.note: to guy someone is to tease or mock them, as is to chaff
an inch is a small measure of length

explanation.surface: A bird is spotted a little way behind some man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'behind' puts the short distance after the word for guy. Guy here is the verb, to make fun of, not a man.
explanation.definitionFit: A common European finch with a pink breast, a small songbird.

clue.text: Student lacking scholarship appearing more often

definitions.meaning: at Oxford a student without a scholarship or exhibition is so called
a comparative: more frequently met with

explanation.surface: An undergraduate without a bursary keeps turning up.
explanation.walkthrough: At Oxford, a student paying fees without a scholarship was traditionally given this title, in contrast to scholars.
explanation.definitionFit: The Oxford term for a fee-paying undergraduate; also the comparative of an adjective meaning frequent or usual.

clue.text: Furious when gross abridgement's swallowed by some

indicators.note: being swallowed by the word for some means going into its middle

parts.note: some, as in 'have you any?', means any
gr. is the shortened form of gross, the measure of twelve dozen

explanation.surface: Someone is enraged when a crude cut is accepted by a few.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abridgement' tells you to shorten gross to its abbreviation, GR, which sits inside ANY.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe someone in a towering rage.

clue.text: Bravely accepts stewed cups of tea

indicators.note: tea that is stewed has been left brewing too long, so these words are mixed up into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone courageously swallows over-brewed tea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stewed' fits the tea so neatly that it hides its job as the anagram signal on CUPS OF TEA.
explanation.definitionFit: To confront a difficulty courageously is to take it on bravely.

clue.text: Dash up to watch Kirov's latest dancer

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word for dash is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to dash is to run
to eye something is to watch it

indicators.note: the latest of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: Rush along to see the newest performer of the Kirov company.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'up' reverses the dash word; 'to' is a link. The Kirov is the St Petersburg ballet company where this Russian dancer trained before defecting.
explanation.definitionFit: Rudolf of that surname was a celebrated Soviet-born ballet star.

clue.text: Passage covering previous case

indicators.note: the passage word goes round the other piece, covering it

parts.note: a hall is an entrance passage or corridor
old, as in 'my old school', means previous or former

explanation.surface: A corridor hides an earlier legal case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case' looks like a law case in this surface, but it is a bag for luggage.
explanation.definitionFit: A large bag for carrying all sorts of belongings when travelling.

clue.text: Succeeded in prosperous period, or bust?

indicators.note: one piece is put inside the other

parts.note: a boom is a time of rapid economic growth
S is the standard abbreviation for succeeded in family trees

explanation.surface: Did a firm thrive in the good times, or go bankrupt?
explanation.walkthrough: 'bust' in the surface is boom's opposite, going bankrupt, but it is the definition as the chest.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words name a woman's chest or breasts.

clue.text: Ask for special favour, left in "The Black Horse"

indicators.note: the letter goes inside the horse's name

parts.note: Black Bess was the horse of the highwayman Dick Turpin

explanation.surface: A request for a particular kindness is left at a pub called The Black Horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Black Horse' reads as a pub name, but it means the famous mare Black Bess, ridden by the English highwayman Dick Turpin.
explanation.definitionFit: To call down divine grace on someone is to invoke heavenly favour for them.

clue.text: I'm involved in reviewing our last training system

indicators.note: being involved in something means being wrapped up inside it
reviewing suggests looking over and reworking the words our last into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone says they are busy assessing their final training scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reviewing' rearranges OUR LAST to SULATOR, and 'involved in' places IM within it after the S.
explanation.definitionFit: A machine reproducing real conditions, such as a flight cockpit, used for instruction.

clue.text: Clean up puppy, perhaps, a cute little one

parts.note: to mop is to clean a floor or spill up
a puppy is an example of a household pet

explanation.surface: Wipe up after the young dog, a sweet little thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' marks the puppy as one example of the wider class.
explanation.definitionFit: An affectionate word for a small, endearing child.

clue.text: Youngster's wonderful spelling

definitions.meaning: a child's exclamation meaning great or brilliant

explanation.surface: A child's marvellous handwriting test.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spelling' looks like orthography, but it is the casting of spells.
explanation.definitionFit: Children's slang for excellent; also the art of enchantment by spells.

clue.text: It charts rise of empire, and most of fall, after revolution

indicators.note: a revolution turns things round, so the letters are rearranged
most of a word is all but its last letter

explanation.surface: A historical chart shows an empire rising and nearly falling after an uprising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' drops the final letter of fall; the nine letters with EMPIRE are then shuffled by 'after revolution'. 'Rise' is height of land, not an empire's growth.
explanation.definitionFit: A map showing hills and valleys by shading or contours depicts the rise of the land.

clue.text: Such a space journey was booked three years ahead

definitions.text: Such a space journey was booked three years ahead

parts.words: Such a space journey was booked three years ahead
parts.note: the 1968 film and book title begins 2001: A Space ..., a date three years after this 1998 puzzle

explanation.surface: A trip into orbit was reserved three years early.
explanation.walkthrough: Arthur C Clarke's novel '2001: A Space ...' gives the term; printed in 1998, the puzzle sees 2001 as three years ahead, and 'booked' means put into a book.
explanation.definitionFit: A long, eventful journey, named after Homer's epic of Odysseus's voyage home.

clue.text: Jack has to sort out problems, that's clear

parts.note: a jack is a sailor, as is an AB, an able seaman
to solve is to work out the answer to a problem

explanation.surface: Jack must fix the difficulties, that's obvious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clear' looks like an adjective, obvious, but it is a verb: to clear someone of blame.
explanation.definitionFit: To pardon or free someone from guilt or sin is to exonerate them.

clue.text: Whereby one's freed from matter of some gravity

definitions.text: Whereby one's freed from matter of some gravity

parts.words: Whereby one's freed from matter of some gravity
parts.note: read as physics: the speed needed for an object to break free of a planet's gravitational pull

explanation.surface: How a person gets out of a serious affair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'matter of some gravity' sounds like a grave business, but it is a mass with gravitational pull, such as a planet.
explanation.definitionFit: The minimum speed a rocket needs to break free of a body's gravitational field.

clue.text: Try to win, about to grow English type of marrow

indicators.note: the courting word goes round the other piece

parts.note: to court someone is to try to win their affection
to get, as in 'get bigger', is to grow or become

explanation.surface: A gardener tries to raise an English variety of squash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to grow' is a verb phrase, as in 'get rich'; 'about' wraps the courting word round it, and English adds its letter at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A small variety of squash, called zucchini in North America, a young marrow.

clue.text: Like the paperwork resulting from a joint account

definitions.text: Like the paperwork resulting from a joint account

parts.words: Like the paperwork resulting from a joint account
parts.note: read as a shared story or report rather than a bank account held by two people

explanation.surface: Describing the forms that come from a shared bank account.
explanation.walkthrough: 'joint account' suggests banking, but an account is also a written narrative produced by two authors together.
explanation.definitionFit: Describes a text whose writing was shared between two or more authors.

clue.text: Water a mare, maybe, before auction

indicators.note: before places the mother before the auction

parts.note: a dam is a mother animal, and a mare is one example
an auction is a sale

explanation.surface: Give a horse a drink before it is sold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Water' looks like a verb about the mare, but it is the definition: the first man's only drink, a humorous name for plain water.
explanation.definitionFit: A humorous name for plain drinking water, the only drink of the first man in Eden.

clue.text: Marvellous direction of some SF films?

definitions.meaning: science-fiction films head away from Earth into space

explanation.surface: Wonderful work by the director of a few science-fiction movies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'direction' sounds like film directing, but it means the way the action goes: off the planet.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for something superb; literally it means away from Earth, where much science fiction is set.

clue.text: Children can be 'accommodated here for the present

definitions.text: Children can be 'accommodated here for the present

parts.words: Children can be 'accommodated here for the present
parts.note: read as a place where a gift for a child can be found, not a temporary home

explanation.surface: Children may be housed here for now.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for the present' sounds like for the time being, but it means for a gift, and 'accommodated' means catered for.
explanation.definitionFit: A shop selling playthings, where a child's gift is bought.

clue.text: Popular shares available for immediate sale

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
stock is shares in a company

explanation.surface: Popular equities can be bought right now.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is stock market talk, but stock here is goods kept by a shop.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods held on the premises ready for purchase are on hand to be bought.

clue.text: Fast food outlet for craftsman

definitions.meaning: British slang for a fish-and-chip shop

explanation.surface: A takeaway for a skilled worker.
explanation.walkthrough: Both senses are British informal: a fish-and-chip shop, and a carpenter, who chips wood.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang both for a fried fish shop and for a joiner or carpenter.

clue.text: On a trip, needs method to find route

parts.note: someone on a drug trip is said to be high
a way of doing something is a method

explanation.surface: Someone on holiday needs a means of finding their way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trip' reads as a journey, fitting 'route', but it is a drug experience.
explanation.definitionFit: A main road is a route between towns.

clue.text: Injury given a twist

definitions.meaning: a cut or other damage to the body
past tense of wind, as of a clock or thread

explanation.surface: A hurt made worse by twisting.
explanation.walkthrough: The two senses are spelt alike but said differently: one rhymes with 'tuned', the other with 'round'.
explanation.definitionFit: A cut or gash in the flesh; also the past participle of wind, coiled or turned.

clue.text: This spinner gets the wind up — second one in panic

definitions.text: This spinner gets the wind up

indicators.note: the numeral goes inside the word for panic

parts.note: alarm is sudden fear or panic
the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: This spinning bowler gets nervous, a moment of fright.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets the wind up' means becomes scared, but here the spinner is a windmill part driven by the wind.
explanation.definitionFit: One of the vanes of a windmill, turned round by the wind.

clue.text: Low joint causes resentment, barring outsiders

indicators.note: barring, meaning excluding, the outside letters drops the first and last letters

parts.note: something that rankles causes lasting bitterness

explanation.surface: A cheap pub upsets people by refusing strangers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Low joint' looks like a seedy bar; it is a joint low on the body. The first and last letters of RANKLES go.
explanation.definitionFit: The joint between foot and leg, the lowest major joint of the limb.

clue.text: By close of play, he was dominating in partnership

definitions.text: By close of play, he was dominating in partnership

parts.words: By close of play, he was dominating in partnership
parts.note: close of play suggests cricket, but it means the end of a stage play in which a husband tames his wife

explanation.surface: By stumps, a batsman was in charge of a stand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'close of play' and 'partnership' are cricket terms, but the play is Shakespeare's The Taming of the Shrew, whose hero has mastered his wife, Katherina, by its end.
explanation.definitionFit: The suitor in Shakespeare's comedy who tames the shrewish Katherina into an obedient wife.

clue.text: The heart, it's said, of spicy Indian cooking

indicators.note: it's said marks that the word for heart is heard, not spelt

parts.note: ticker is slang for the heart

explanation.surface: Curry is said to be the heart of Indian cuisine.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic British accent the slang word sounds just like the dish.
explanation.definitionFit: A dish of meat marinated in spices and cooked in pieces, as in chicken tikka.

clue.text: Give up and return

definitions.meaning: a profit or output from an investment or crop

explanation.surface: Surrender and go back.
explanation.definitionFit: To surrender or concede; also the profit an investment produces.

clue.text: Doing one's best with ease, knocking out aces from China

indicators.note: knocking out means removing letters from the words before it

parts.note: peaking is reaching one's highest level
ease means comfort
A is the card abbreviation for ace, so two aces are two A's

explanation.surface: A tennis player, on top form and at ease, stops serving aces against China.
explanation.walkthrough: One A comes out of PEAKING and one from EASE, leaving PEKING and ESE. 'from China' is the definition: an adjective for the toy dog breed's origin, or a person from Beijing.
explanation.definitionFit: Means of or from Beijing, the Chinese capital once spelt Peking.
